payload.answer: Originally shipped: 96 units (12 cartons × 8 units per carton). Usable units remaining: 93 (96 − 3 damaged units). Limitation: this treats the reported three damaged units as part of this shipment and assumes no other losses or unusable units.

approaches.description: Multiply the dispatched-carton count by the shipment-specific units per carton, then subtract the recorded damaged units.
approaches.reason: All three supplied records concern the shipment, but the records do not explicitly rule out other losses.

claims.statement: The dispatch record reports that 12 cartons were shipped.
The packing specification states that each carton in this shipment contains 8 units.

citations.quote: 3 units were damaged in transit and are not usable.

claims.statement: The receiving record reports 3 unusable units damaged in transit.

claims.basis_reference: Derived in step-shipped-units from the carton count and carton capacity.
Assume the recorded three damaged units belong to the 96 shipped units and no additional unrecorded losses affect usability.
claims.statement: Under the stated assumption, 93 usable units remain.

open_questions: The records do not explicitly state whether there were other losses, shortages, or unusable units beyond the three damaged units.

proof_steps.justification: By multiplication, 12 cartons × 8 units per carton = 96 units.
proof_steps.statement: Compute the original shipment quantity as 96 units.

proof_steps.justification: Assuming the 3 recorded damaged units are included in the 96 shipped units and are the only unusable units, subtract: 96 − 3 = 93.
proof_steps.statement: Compute the remaining usable quantity as 93 units.
